Histor · The evidence layer for autonomous AI (https://histor.dev/) citeturn77search0 [wordlim: 200] Crawled: 3 weeks ago; Patent pending # The evidence layer for autonomous AI. Histor is an independent witness for AI agents. When an agent reads from any HTTPS server, Histor co-signs a receipt of exactly what that server sent. The agent’s own operator can’t forge it or edit it later, and anyone can check it offline. agents that can prove what they saw agent → TLS session → witness co-signs → receipt → anyone verifies Any HTTPS server Nothing to install on it ~10 ms offline check Histor receipt ### What the server sent recorded run Houston Hobby · KHOU valid server api.weather.gov request GET /stations/KHOU/…/latest session 2026-09-30 07:52:13 UTC sky Mostly Clear temp 27 °C wind 12.96 km/h witness 028e23f6…f43d · secp256k1 receipt sha256:3d40d10d…05ba rest of response: hidden offline check verification path certificate → commitment → witness $ histor verify --trust 028e23f6…f43d \   --receipt-file genuine.json valid: true · exit 0 ### Agent builders Your agent hands another agent, a customer or an auditor a receipt for what an API said. They check it offline and act on it, without trusting you. See the developer tools ### Insurers and MGAs AI-liability cover runs on agent logs the insured writes. A Histor receipt is evidence the insured did not write and cannot edit. What insurers get ### Risk and platform teams Agents that move money or change records leave a trail your own staff cannot rewrite, checkable by anyone with the witness key. Talk to us about a pilot The gap ## An agent’s log is its operator’s word. Agents now move money, file records and act on data they fetched. When something goes wrong, the only record of what the agent saw is a log the operator wrote, and the operator can write anything into it. API providers don’t sign their responses, so there is nothing to check that log against. An agent log today * Written by the operator, after the fact. * Editable by anyone with access to the logs. * Signing it later stops backdating, but the false entry was made at the start. * Insurers, auditors and other agents take it on trust. A Histor receipt * Co-signed during the session by a witness the operator doesn’t control. * Fixed bytes. Change one and verification fails. * Names the server through its public web certificate. * Checked offline in about 10 ms, with no call to Histor. How it works ## What a receipt does not prove. A receipt proves what a named server sent, and when. Read it as exactly that. It does not prove * That the server told the truth. A receipt shows what api.weather.gov said, not the weather. * Anything about a server the operator controls. That receipt is still the operator’s word, now fixed in time and bytes. * That the agent sent every action through the witness. That takes credential custody or egress control. * Independence, when one party runs both the agent side and the witness. High-value receipts should carry more than one witness. * That the content is safe to act on. A genuine page can still carry a prompt injection. Engine limits today: TLS 1.2 only (TLS 1.3 is on TLSNotary’s roadmap), pre-release software, and no compressed or streamed responses. ## Two tools your agent already knows how to call. Histor ships as a CLI and an MCP server, so it works in Claude Code, Cursor and any MCP client. Receipts are content-addressed: agents pass a short receipt_id instead of 15 KB of base64. witnessed_fetch(url, fields?, mode?) GETs an https:// URL through a Histor witness. Returns the server, time, request and disclosed fields, plus a receipt_id. verify_receipt(receipt_id | receipt, expect_server?) Checks a receipt another agent handed you, offline. Returns what it proves, or the reason it fails. witnessed_request(url, method, body, request_fields?) POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE. Credentials for the target live on the server, so the model never sees a secret. The request body is committed and stays hidden unless you disclose named fields. [Button: MCP config][Button: CLI] Copy { "mcpServers": { "histor": { "command": "node", "args": ["histor-mcp/server.mjs"], "env": { "HISTOR_WITNESS": "", "HISTOR_TRUST": "" } } } } Private beta. The CLI and MCP server are released to pilot teams first. Request beta access For insurers and MGAs ## Underwrite from evidence the insured didn’t write. New AI-liability covers ask for agent logs, and today those logs are self-reported. Cyber insurers learned to price from external scans the insured couldn’t edit. A Histor receipt gives an AI-liability book the same kind of signal for agent actions. ### At claim time Check what the agent was told before it acted. The claims desk verifies the receipt itself, offline. ### At underwriting Witnessed actions as a share of all agent actions is a number the insured can’t inflate. ### Narrow by design A receipt proves what a named server sent and when. It makes no claim about whether the agent acted well. Talk to us about a program pilot Pricing ## Free to read. Paid to act. Free reads let receipts spread between agents. Writes, extra witnesses and dedicated capacity pay for the network. Witnessed reads Free On the hosted witness, rate-limited. Witnessed writes 2¢ Per call that changes something: POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE. Two-witness receipts +1¢ For high-value actions, once a second independent operator is live. Design-partner pilot $10,000 60 days. Setup, 250,000 witnessed actions and an evidence report your insurer can read. Dedicated or self-hosted witness Talk to us Your own witness key and capacity, with more than one witness for high-value actions. Security ## Built so you don’t have to trust us. The verifier needs the witness’s public key and the public web certificate roots. It never calls Histor, so a receipt keeps working even if Histor is gone. ### Two trust anchors A compressed secp256k1 witness key and the public web PKI. Nothing else. ### Secrets stay put Credentials for writes live on the server. Disclosure is fail-closed: a field that contains a credential cannot be revealed. ### Public targets only The witness resolves names itself and refuses loopback, private and cloud-metadata addresses. ### Open protocol Receipts are TLSNotary presentations. Signed statements are being mapped to COSE for IETF SCITT transparency services. ### Where things stand Updated 1 October 2026 Forge-at-birth proof Working Runs against the live api.weather.gov feed. 3 of 3 rounds behave as expected. histor CLI Built witness, fetch, verify. GET and writes, MPC and proxy modes, 20 unit tests passing. MCP server Built stdio and Streamable HTTP. Private beta. Hosted witness Built, not live Container built and tested. Its public key is published here the day it goes live. Second, independent witness operator Planned Until then, hosted receipts are labeled Histor-attested. Hardware-backed witness tier Planned Found a security issue? Email founder@verdict.systems with “Histor security” in the subject. Pilot access ## Bring us the agent action you most need to prove. Design-partner pilots run 60 days. We set up the witness, run your agents’ calls through it, and hand you a report your risk team or insurer can check on their own. This form opens an email in your own mail app. Nothing is stored on this site. If a borrower had previous mortgages, the lender does not have to independently verify the mortgage’s payment history provided the credit report includes a reference to the mortgage (or mortgages) and reflects 12 months of the most recent payment activity. If adequate mortgage payment history is not included in the borrower’s credit report, the lender must use the following to verify the borrower’s payment history on a previous mortgage(s): - a standard mortgage verification; - loan payment history from the servicer; - the borrower’s canceled checks for the last 12 months; or - the borrower’s year-end mortgage account statement, provided the statement includes a payment receipt history, and, if applicable, canceled checks for the months elapsed since the year-end mortgage account statement was issued. # Standard Mortgage Verifications from Servicers When a lender relies on standard mortgage verifications from servicers or holders, it must ensure that the verifications include: - the unpaid principal balance of the mortgage and monthly payment amount; - the present status of the mortgage, such as current, 30 days’ delinquent, etc.; and - the borrower’s payment history. When a servicer fails to provide all of the requested information, the lender must rely on information provided through the borrower’s canceled checks. The checks must: - be legible, - identify the mortgage servicer or mortgage holder as the payee, - indicate that the servicer or holder endorsed the check for deposit, and - indicate the date the servicer or holder deposited the check. # Existing Mortgage Payment Requirements Published March 6, 2024 465-------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Docs: chain facts, contracts and the public API | Jevmaxxing (https://jevmaxxing.trade/docs) citeturn77search5 [wordlim: 200] Crawled: 2 weeks ago; ## Live now, and what arrives with the token Live today: SCOUT, WARDEN, PULSE, LEDGER and FLUX all read Robinhood Chain directly, Jev answers through the gateway, receipts are published, and the snipe ticket is signed in your own wallet. NYU says the model ranked risk better than tested single-scan approaches. The retrospective study used one health system and equipment manufacturer; external testing is pending, and the research tool is not FDA-authorized for clinical use. Read full story → +26 Net Positive ▲Opportunity 58/100 Repeated 3D mammograms improved five-year risk ranking in a large retrospective NYU dataset, supporting research into more individualized screening without requiring another scan. The measured benefit concerns risk discrimination, not demonstrated patient outcomes. ▼Risk 32/100 One health system and imaging manufacturer limit generalizability, and external and prospective testing are pending.
